problem: Existing modular Embodied Instruction Following (EIF) methods on ALFRED struggle with small-object navigation because exploration is ineffective and perception (segmentation and depth) is imperfect.
motivation: Small target objects are hard to find and to perceive, so failures in exploration and perception limit overall task success. The paper uses common-sense knowledge from seen scenes and cues in the language instructions to guide exploration, and hierarchical features to improve dense perception.
key_idea: Combine Common Sense Language-guided exploration (CSL), which infers likely object locations from seen-scene common sense and instruction information, with Hierarchical Dense Perception (HDP), which uses hierarchical features for joint semantic segmentation and depth estimation.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that better exploration efficiency (CSL) and better perception (HDP) each contribute to the gains on ALFRED.
method: Common Sense Language-guided exploration (CSL): uses common-sense knowledge from seen scenes plus information in the language instruction to infer where the target object is, guiding exploration and improving efficiency.
Hierarchical Dense Perception (HDP): uses hierarchical features to perform semantic segmentation and depth estimation, improving the agent's perception.

setting.backbone: not specified in abstract (learned segmentation/depth perception module plus CSL exploration)

numbers_note: abstract only; the abstract gives only an absolute improvement of 9.29% (18.45% relative) on unseen test scenes over the previous state of the art, with no raw metric values.
results: CSL-HDP achieves an absolute improvement of 9.29% (18.45% relative) on ALFRED unseen test scenes over the previous state of the art and ranks first on the leaderboard.
limitations: Abstract only, so limitations are not stated.
The focus on small-object navigation may limit generality beyond ALFRED.
